title: Easter Island: Mystery, Moai, and the Edge of the World
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

keywords.def: Far away from other places, especially cities or populated areas.
Related to the people who settled many Pacific islands, including Easter Island.
A person skilled at finding routes across land or sea, especially over long distances.
A person from whom one is descended, often honoured in traditional societies.
A large family group sharing common ancestors.
The breakdown or failure of a society or system.
Cultural traditions, objects, and history passed down through generations.

sentences.en: Imagine living in a place so remote that the nearest inhabited land is over two thousand kilometres away.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，生活在一个如此偏远的地方，最近的有人居住的陆地也在两千多公里之外。

sentences.en: No neighbours. No easy escape. Just ocean in every direction.
sentences.zh: 没有邻居，没有轻易逃离的可能，四面八方只有茫茫大海。

sentences.en: And across the island are hundreds of giant stone heads, carved by hand.
sentences.zh: 而在这座岛屿的各处，耸立着数百尊由人工雕刻的巨型石像。

sentences.en: This place exists… and people have lived there for centuries.
sentences.zh: 这个地方确实存在，而且人们在那里已经生活了几个世纪。

sentences.en: This episode will look at Easter Island, or Rapa Nui as it is known locally.
sentences.zh: 本期节目将带大家了解复活节岛，也就是当地人所称的 Rapa Nui。

sentences.en: Easter Island is in the middle of the Pacific Ocean, one of the most isolated inhabited islands on Earth, and home to hundreds of giant stone heads.
sentences.zh: 复活节岛位于太平洋中部，是地球上最孤立的有人居住的岛屿之一，也是数百尊巨型石像的故乡。

sentences.en: So how did humans even get here? How did people cross vast oceans, reach this tiny volcanic island, and then decide to stay?
sentences.zh: 那么，人类当初是怎么到达这里的呢？人们是如何跨越浩瀚的海洋，抵达这座微小的火山岛，并决定留下来呢？

sentences.en: And how did they organise a society capable of carving and moving some of the largest stone statues ever created?
sentences.zh: 他们又是如何组织起一个能够雕刻和搬运史上最大石像之一的社会的呢？

sentences.en: In today’s episode of Thinking in English, we’re travelling to the edge of the world to explore one of the most fascinating human stories ever told.
sentences.zh: 在今天的《Thinking in English》节目中，我们将前往世界边缘，探索人类历史上最迷人的故事之一。

sentences.en: And we’ll learn some English vocabulary along the way!
sentences.zh: 我们还会在旅途中学习一些英语词汇！

sentences.en: Where exactly is Easter Island? Geographically, Easter Island sits in the Southeastern Pacific Ocean.
sentences.zh: 复活节岛到底在哪里？从地理上看，复活节岛坐落在东南太平洋。

sentences.en: On a map, it almost looks like a mistake.
sentences.zh: 在地图上，它看起来几乎像是个错误。

sentences.en: It is a tiny triangle of land floating alone in a massive blue space.
sentences.zh: 它是一小片孤零零地漂浮在广阔蓝色虚空中的三角形陆地。

sentences.en: Today, it’s officially a territory of Chile, but that doesn’t mean it’s close to Chile.
sentences.zh: 如今，它官方上是智利的一个领地，但这并不意味着它离智利很近。

sentences.en: In fact, mainland Chile is over 3,500 kilometers away.
sentences.zh: 事实上，智利本土距离这里有3500多公里。

sentences.en: To put that into perspective, if you traveled from London to Moscow, you’d still be closer to home than Easter Island is to Chile.
sentences.zh: 换位思考一下，如果你从伦敦旅行到莫斯科，你距离家的距离依然比复活节岛距离智利要近。

sentences.en: The closest inhabited island to Easter Island is Pitcairn Island, which is more than 2000 kilometers away.
sentences.zh: 距离复活节岛最近的有人居住的岛屿是皮特凯恩岛，距离超过2000公里。

sentences.en: And Pitcairn Island is also one of the most isolated places on earth, with a tiny population.
sentences.zh: 而且皮特凯恩岛也是地球上人口极其稀少的最孤立地方之一。

sentences.en: I actually have an old episode about Pitcairn Island.
sentences.zh: 我其实做过一期关于皮特凯恩岛的老节目。

sentences.en: Everywhere you look around Easter Island, there is ocean.
sentences.zh: 无论你在复活节岛周围看哪里，全都是海洋。

sentences.en: There are no nearby islands. There’s just water.
sentences.zh: 附近没有别的岛屿，只有水。

sentences.en: When a group of people or a community lives in a place so remote, everything becomes important.
sentences.zh: 当一个群体或社区生活在这样一个偏远的地方时，一切都变得至关重要。

sentences.en: Trees and food, fresh water, and the survival of people are vital.
sentences.zh: 树木与食物、淡水以及人们的生存都是至关重要的。

sentences.en: There’s no easy way to leave. And there’s no simple way to recover from an emergency or a disaster.
sentences.zh: 这里没有轻松离开的方式，也没有从紧急情况或灾难中简单恢复的办法。

sentences.en: I should also talk a little bit about the name.
sentences.zh: 我还应该稍微聊聊这个名字的由来。

sentences.en: In most European languages, the island is called “Easter Island “.
sentences.zh: 在大多数欧洲语言中，这座岛被称为“Easter Island”。

sentences.en: It is now part of Chile, a Spanish speaking country, so commonly called Isla de Pascua, which probably I’ve mispronounced, but means “Easter Island” in Spanish.
sentences.zh: 它现在是智利的一部分，智利是一个西班牙语国家，所以通常被称为 Isla de Pascua，这个发音我可能读得不太准，但在西班牙语里就是“复活节岛”的意思。

sentences.en: However, the Polynesian name for the island is Rapa Nui, which means “Big Nui.” And the term Rapa Nui is also used to refer to the people of the island as well.
sentences.zh: 然而，这座岛的波利尼西亚语名称是 Rapa Nui，意思是“大尼ui”。“Rapa Nui”这个词也被用来指代岛上的居民。

sentences.en: So in this episode, I will use Easter Island and Rapa Nui to describe the island.
sentences.zh: 所以在今天的节目中，我会交替使用复活节岛和 Rapa Nui 来描述这座岛。

sentences.en: The people of Easter Island are Polynesian.
sentences.zh: 复活节岛的人民是波利尼西亚人。

sentences.en: Polynesians were a group of seafaring people whose ancestors originally came from Southeast Asia.
sentences.zh: 波利尼西亚人是一群航海民族，他们的祖先最初来自东南亚。

sentences.en: Over thousands of years, they gradually moved eastwards into the Pacific Ocean.
sentences.zh: 经过数千年的时间，他们逐渐向东迁徙进入太平洋。

sentences.en: They settled on islands that were separated by vast distances of open water.
sentences.zh: 他们在被广阔开阔水域隔开的岛屿上定居。

sentences.en: This was a long process of migration and expansion.
sentences.zh: 这是一个漫长的迁徙与扩张过程。

sentences.en: From their early centers in Taiwan, and then the Philippines, the Polynesian people spread through Melanesia and into the Central Pacific.
sentences.zh: 从他们早期的中心台湾，然后是菲律宾，波利尼西亚人通过美拉尼西亚扩散到了中太平洋。

sentences.en: By around the year 1000, Polynesians had settled islands across what is called the Polynesian Triangle.
sentences.zh: 大约在公元1000年左右，波利尼西亚人已经在被称为波利尼西亚三角区的各个岛屿上定居。

sentences.en: This includes Hawaii in the north, New Zealand in the south, and Easter Island in the east.
sentences.zh: 这包括北部的夏威夷、南部的纽西兰（新西兰），以及东部的复活节岛。

sentences.en: Along the way, they settled and developed cultures in places like Tahiti, Samoa, Tonga, and the Cook Islands.
sentences.zh: 一路上，他们在塔希提、萨摩亚、汤加和库克群岛等地定居并发展了文化。

sentences.en: Polynesians were among the greatest navigators the world has ever known.
sentences.zh: 波利尼西亚人是世界上最伟大的航海家之一。

sentences.en: They crossed thousands of kilometers of open ocean in a large double-hulled canoes without compasses, maps, or modern instruments.
sentences.zh: 他们驾驶着大型双体独木舟，在没有指南针、地图或现代仪器的帮助下，横渡了数千公里的开阔海洋。

sentences.en: They often carried plants with them and animals, tools, and took their entire families.
sentences.zh: 他们通常随身携带植物、动物、工具，并带着整个家族。

sentences.en: Sailors memorized the positions of stars and used them as maps.
sentences.zh: 水手们能记住星星的位置，并把它们当作地图来使用。

sentences.en: They followed ocean currents and wave patterns that reflected off distant islands.
sentences.zh: 他们追随洋流和从远方岛屿反射回来的波浪模式。

sentences.en: They observed birds knowing that some species only fly a certain distance from shore.
sentences.zh: 他们观察鸟类，知道某些物种只在离海岸一定距离的范围内飞行。

sentences.en: This knowledge was passed orally, by word, from generation to generation.
sentences.zh: 这种知识是通过口耳相传，一代一代传下来的。

sentences.en: Around the year 1,200, Polynesian sailors reached and settled Easter Island.
sentences.zh: 大约在公元1200年，波利尼西亚水手到达并定居了复活节岛。

sentences.en: By that time, they had almost reached every habitable island in the Pacific, and Easter Island sat at the far eastern edge of the ocean.
sentences.zh: 到那时，他们几乎已经到达了太平洋中所有适合居住的岛屿，而复活节岛则位于海洋的最东端边缘。

sentences.en: Why did these sailors choose to settle somewhere so remote?
sentences.zh: 为什么这些水手会选择在这么偏远的地方定居呢？

sentences.en: Well, there was nowhere else nearby. There were no nearby islands.
sentences.zh: 嗯，附近没有其他地方了，也没有附近的岛屿。

sentences.en: There were limited resources on Easter Island.
sentences.zh: 复活节岛上的资源十分有限。

sentences.en: And no easy way back to where they came from.
sentences.zh: 而且没有轻松回到他们来处的方法。

sentences.en: Some historians suggest population pressure pushed Polynesian people to keep moving.
sentences.zh: 一些历史学家认为，人口压力迫使波利尼西亚人不断前行。

sentences.en: That’s why people kept moving from Tonga to Samoa, to Hawaii, to New Zealand, to Easter Island.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么人们不断从汤加迁移到萨摩亚、夏威夷、新西兰，再到复活节岛。

sentences.en: Other historians argue that exploration itself was a central part of Polynesian culture.
sentences.zh: 另一些历史学家则认为，探索本身就是波利尼西亚文化的核心部分。

sentences.en: Discovering new land, brought status, brought power.
sentences.zh: 发现新的土地能带来地位和权力。

sentences.en: Whatever the reason, the people who reached Easter Island were not lost or accidental survivors.
sentences.zh: 无论原因是什么，到达复活节岛的人并不是迷路者或偶然的幸存者。

sentences.en: They didn’t accidentally appear on Easter Island.
sentences.zh: 他们不是偶然出现在复活节岛上的。

sentences.en: They were skilled seafarers and they deliberately chose to settle on one of the most remote islands in the world.
sentences.zh: 他们是熟练的航海家，并且是故意选择在世界上最偏远的岛屿之一定居的。

sentences.en: Before we move on to talk more about Easter Island, I think it would be interesting to take a slight detour here.
sentences.zh: 在我们继续深入探讨复活节岛之前，我觉得在这里稍微绕个弯会很有趣。

sentences.en: Easter Island, is in the Southeast Pacific Ocean, far from anywhere else.
sentences.zh: 复活节岛位于东南太平洋，远离其他任何地方。

sentences.en: The Polynesians who settled there must have been extremely skilled navigators.
sentences.zh: 在那里定居的波利尼西亚人一定是非常娴熟的航海家。

sentences.en: Easter Island is traditionally seen as the last stop the Polynesians made on their journey across the Pacific.
sentences.zh: 传统上，复活节岛被视为波利尼西亚人横渡太平洋之旅的最后一站。

sentences.en: But was it? Did they go further? More specifically, did Polynesians reach South America centuries before Europeans arrived?
sentences.zh: 但真的是这样吗？他们走得更远了吗？更具体地说，波利尼西亚人是否在欧洲人到达前的几个世纪就抵达了南美洲？

sentences.en: This idea has been debated for decades and for a long time it was dismissed as impossible.
sentences.zh: 这个观点已经争论了几十年，很长一段时间里它都被认为是不可能的而遭到否定。

sentences.en: But in recent years, some new evidence has forced historians to take the question seriously.
sentences.zh: 但在最近几年，一些新的证据迫使历史学家认真对待这个问题。

sentences.en: It’s still a very uncertain topic, but I find it fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这依然是一个非常不确定的课题，但我发现它十分引人入胜。

sentences.en: One of the most interesting clues is the sweet potato.
sentences.zh: 其中一个最有趣的线索就是红薯（甘薯）。

sentences.en: Sweet potatoes are native to South America, but when Europeans first arrived in Polynesia, they found sweet potatoes already being grown on islands across the Pacific.
sentences.zh: 红薯原产于南美洲，但当欧洲人首次抵达波利尼西亚时，他们发现红薯已经在太平洋各岛屿上种植了。

sentences.en: One explanation is that Polynesians themselves reached the coast of South America, collected the plant, and brought it back with them.
sentences.zh: 一种解释是，波利尼西亚人自己到达了南美洲海岸，采集了这种植物，并把它带了回来。

sentences.en: Some scientific research also suggests genetic contact between Polynesian populations and indigenous peoples of South America, dating to around the 13th century.
sentences.zh: 一些科学研究还表明，波利尼西亚人群与南美洲原住民之间存在基因交流，时间可以追溯到大约13世纪。

sentences.en: Basically, when people do DNA tests of indigenous South Americans, they have a tiny amount of Polynesian DNA as well.
sentences.zh: 基本上，当人们对南美洲原住民进行DNA检测时，会发现他们身上也带有极少量的波利尼西亚DNA。

sentences.en: While this doesn’t prove large-scale migration, it does point to the fact there may have been some Polynesian people in South America.
sentences.zh: 虽然这不能证明大规模的迁徙，但它确实表明当时可能确实有波利尼西亚人去过南美洲。

sentences.en: There are also similarities in tools and fishing techniques, and some of the design patterns found on both sides of the Pacific.
sentences.zh: 双方在工具、捕鱼技术以及太平洋两岸发现的一些设计图案上也有相似之处。

sentences.en: On their own, these similarities are not evidence.
sentences.zh: 单看这些相似之处并不能构成证据。

sentences.en: But taken together, it suggests there may have been some interaction or contact.
sentences.zh: 但综合起来看，这暗示着双方可能存在某种互动或接触。

sentences.en: But as I said, this is a very controversial and conspiracy-theory-laden topic, but I find it really interesting to think that these Polynesian sailors may have been in contact with South America hundreds of years before Europe.
sentences.zh: 但正如我所说，这是一个充满争议且带有阴谋论色彩的话题，不过一想到这些波利尼西亚水手可能在欧洲人到来几百年前就与南美洲有过接触，我就觉得非常有趣。

sentences.en: So let’s go back to Easter Island. When people think of Easter Island, they usually think of the giant stone heads.
sentences.zh: 那么让我们回到复活节岛。当人们想到复活节岛时，通常都会想到巨大的石像。

sentences.en: These statues are known as Moai. I think I’m pronouncing that correctly.
sentences.zh: 这些雕像被称为 Moai。我觉得我的发音应该挺准确的。

sentences.en: The Moai are one of the most recognizable monuments in the world.
sentences.zh: Moai 是世界上辨识度最高的纪念碑之一。

sentences.en: They were carved between the years 1250 and 1500, and there are more than 900 of them scattered across the island.
sentences.zh: 它们雕刻于公元1250年至1500年之间，全岛散落着900多尊这样的石像。

sentences.en: Most were carved from volcanic rock using only stone tools.
sentences.zh: 大多数石像是仅用石器从火山岩中雕刻出来的。

sentences.en: Despite how they’re often described, Moai are not just heads.
sentences.zh: 尽管人们经常这样描述，但 Moai 并不只是脑袋。

sentences.en: Many of them have bodies buried beneath the ground.
sentences.zh: 它们的许多身体都埋在地下。

sentences.en: And some once had large red stone hats that were placed on top.
sentences.zh: 有些石像的顶部曾经还戴着巨大的红色石帽。

sentences.en: They were positioned on stone platforms near villages, and most of them faced inland, not out to sea.
sentences.zh: 它们被安置在村庄附近的石质平台上，而且大多数都面向内陆，而不是面向大海。

sentences.en: This is because the Moai were believed to represent ancestors or powerful leaders.
sentences.zh: 这是因为人们相信 Moai 代表着祖先或强有力的领袖。

sentences.en: They were watching over the people. Rapa Nui society was organized around families and clans.
sentences.zh: 它们在守护着人民。Rapa Nui 的社会是以家庭和氏族为组织结构的。

sentences.en: Daily life involved fishing and farming, tool making, and religious rituals.
sentences.zh: 日常生活包括捕鱼和耕作、制造工具以及宗教仪式。

sentences.en: With very limited land and very limited resources, cooperation across the island was essential.
sentences.zh: 在土地和资源都非常有限的情况下，全岛的合作至关重要。

sentences.en: But there was also competition. Building Moai became a way for clans to demonstrate their power and honor their ancestors.
sentences.zh: 但竞争也同样存在。建造 Moai 成了各个氏族展示权力和缅怀祖先的一种方式。

sentences.en: There are lots of mysteries around the Moai.
sentences.zh: 关于 Moai 有着许多谜团。

sentences.en: How were these enormous statues moved across the island without wheels, tools, or animals?
sentences.zh: 在没有轮子、工具或动物的情况下，这些巨大的石像是如何在岛上被运送的呢？

sentences.en: Some Moai weigh more than 70 tons. One theory suggests that they were laid flat and dragged on wooden sleds.
sentences.zh: 有些 Moai 的重量超过70吨。有一种理论认为，它们是被放倒并用木质雪橇拖拽的。

sentences.en: Another argues that they were walked upright using ropes, rocking them forward step by step.
sentences.zh: 另一种观点则认为，它们是利用绳索直立“行走”的，通过一步步左右摇晃向前移动。

sentences.en: And experiments have shown that that might be possible.
sentences.zh: 而实验已经证明，这种方法是可能的。

sentences.en: For many years, the story of Easter Island has been told as a warning.
sentences.zh: 多年来，复活节岛的故事一直被当作一个警示寓言来讲述。

sentences.en: It was described as a society that destroyed its own environment and collapsed as a result.
sentences.zh: 它被描述为一个破坏了自身环境并因此走向崩溃的社会。

sentences.en: According to this idea, the island’s forests were destroyed to move the Moai, leading to soil erosion, food shortages, and eventually social breakdown.
sentences.zh: 根据这种观点，岛上的森林为了搬运 Moai 被砍伐殆尽，导致了水土流失、粮食短缺，最终引发了社会崩溃。

sentences.en: More recent research, however, suggests a much more complex picture.
sentences.zh: 然而，更近的研究表明情况要复杂得多。

sentences.en: Life on Easter Island was always fragile.
sentences.zh: 复活节岛上的生活一直都是脆弱的。

sentences.en: The island was small, isolated, and very limited in resources.
sentences.zh: 这座岛屿面积狭小、孤立，资源非常有限。

sentences.en: Over time, deforestation did reduce the number of trees available for building and farming and fuel.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，森林砍伐确实减少了可用于建造、农业和燃料的树木数量。

sentences.en: As a result, soil quality did decline and food became harder to produce.
sentences.zh: 结果，土壤质量确实下降了，粮食也变得更难生产。

sentences.en: When resources are scarce, tensions grow.
sentences.zh: 当资源匮乏时，紧张局势就会加剧。

sentences.en: Competition between clans increased. Some archeologists believe this period saw rising internal conflict.
sentences.zh: 氏族之间的竞争加剧了。一些考古学家认为，这一时期见证了内部冲突的上升。

sentences.en: In 1722, Dutch ships became the first Europeans to reach Easter Island.
sentences.zh: 1722年，荷兰船只成为第一批到达复活节岛的欧洲人。

sentences.en: The Europeans first spotted the island on Easter Sunday and gave it the name Easter Island.
sentences.zh: 欧洲人在复活节当天首次发现了这座岛，并将其命名为复活节岛。

sentences.en: This is very similar to Christmas Island, which I recorded an episode on a few months ago, which was named on Christmas Day.
sentences.zh: 这与几个月前我录过一期节目的圣诞岛非常相似，圣诞岛就是在圣诞节那天被命名的。

sentences.en: Over the next century, more European ships arrived.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的一个世纪里，更多的欧洲船只抵达了这里。

sentences.en: They brought with them diseases to which the Rapa Nui had no immunity.
sentences.zh: 他们带来了 Rapa Nui 人毫无免疫力的疾病。

sentences.en: Things like smallpox and tuberculosis, and influenza.
sentences.zh: 比如天花、结核病和流感。

sentences.en: These diseases spread rapidly and killed a large number of the population.
sentences.zh: 这些疾病迅速蔓延，夺去了大量人口的生命。

sentences.en: Even worse was the impact of slavery. In the 19th century, slave traders kidnapped hundreds of Rapa Nui people and forced them to work in mines and plantations in South America.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是奴隶贸易带来的冲击。在19世纪，奴隶贩子绑架了数百名 Rapa Nui 人，强迫他们在南美洲的矿山和种植园里劳作。

sentences.en: Very few of these people ever returned. Those who did brought diseases back with them causing further devastation.
sentences.zh: 这些人中极少数能够活着回来。那些回来的人把疾病也带了回来，造成了进一步的毁灭。

sentences.en: By the late 1800s, the population of Easter Island had collapsed to just a few hundred people.
sentences.zh: 到了19世纪末，复活节岛的人口已经锐减到仅剩几百人。

sentences.en: This wasn’t just the result of poor decisions.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是糟糕决策的结果。

sentences.en: This was also the result of violence and exploitation, and neglect.
sentences.zh: 这也是暴力、剥削和忽视所导致的后果。

sentences.en: After disease, slavery and population collapse, the Rapa Nui people were left with little power to resist outside control.
sentences.zh: 在经历疾病、奴隶制和人口崩溃之后，Rapa Nui 人几乎失去了抵抗外部控制的力量。

sentences.en: In 1888, Chile officially annexed Easter Island.
sentences.zh: 1888年，智利正式吞并了复活节岛。

sentences.en: This means they turned it into a Chilean territory.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们将其变成了智利的领地。

sentences.en: Most of the island’s land was leased to foreign companies, mainly for sheep farming.
sentences.zh: 岛上的大部分土地被租给外国公司，主要用于养羊。

sentences.en: And the local population were restricted to a small area of the island.
sentences.zh: 而当地居民则被限制在岛上的一个小区域内。

sentences.en: For many years, the Rapa Nui language was discouraged or banned in schools.
sentences.zh: 多年来，Rapa Nui 语在学校里受到排挤或禁止使用。

sentences.en: Traditional practices were ignored or replaced, and decisions about the island were made in Chile, not on Easter Island.
sentences.zh: 传统习俗被忽视或取代，关于这座岛屿的决策是在智利做出，而不是在复活节岛上。

sentences.en: While Easter Island is legally part of Chile, many of the Rapa Nui people see themselves not as Chilean, but as Rapa Nui.
sentences.zh: 虽然复活节岛在法律上是智利的一部分，但许多 Rapa Nui 人并不把自己看作智利人，而是看作 Rapa Nui 人。

sentences.en: They have their own history, their own identity, and their own rights.
sentences.zh: 他们有自己的历史、自己的身份认同和自己的权利。

sentences.en: Today, Rapa Nui is home to around 8,000 people, many of whom are descendants of the original inhabitants.
sentences.zh: 如今，Rapa Nui 居住着大约8000人，其中许多人都是最初居民的后代。

sentences.en: Tourism is now the main source of income.
sentences.zh: 旅游业现在是主要的收入来源。

sentences.en: Visitors come from all over the world to see the Moai or walk in the beautiful landscapes or experience the traditional culture.
sentences.zh: 来自世界各地的游客前来观赏 Moai，漫步于美丽的风景中，或体验传统文化。

sentences.en: This brings opportunities and pressure. Too many visitors can cause damage.
sentences.zh: 这既带来了机遇，也带来了压力。过多的游客可能会造成破坏。

sentences.en: At the same time, Easter Island has experienced somewhat of a cultural revival.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，复活节岛也经历了一定程度的文化复兴。

sentences.en: The Rapa Nui language is now taught in schools.
sentences.zh: Rapa Nui 语现在已经在学校里教授了。

sentences.en: Traditional music and dance and tattooing have returned to the island.
sentences.zh: 传统的音乐、舞蹈和纹身又回到了岛上。

sentences.en: And environmental protection is the priority.
sentences.zh: 环境保护被放在了首位。

sentences.en: The island faces massive challenges from climate change, plastic pollution, and limited resources.
sentences.zh: 这座岛屿正面临着气候变化、塑料污染以及资源有限等巨大挑战。

sentences.en: After all of this history, I think I’d like to end this episode with a little bit of a debate.
sentences.zh: 在回顾了所有这些历史之后，我觉得本期节目可以用一场小小的辩论来收尾。

sentences.en: Across the world museums display artifacts taken from colonized or occupied societies.
sentences.zh: 世界各地的博物馆都陈列着从被殖民或被占领社会掠夺来的文物。

sentences.en: Easter Island is no exception. Several Moai and important Rapa Nui objects are held in foreign museums, including the famous Moai statue in the British Museum.
sentences.zh: 复活节岛也不例外。几尊 Moai 和重要的 Rapa Nui 文物被保存在外国博物馆中，其中包括大英博物馆里那尊著名的 Moai 雕像。

sentences.en: The first time I visited the British Museum in London as a child, my favorite exhibit was the Moai.
sentences.zh: 我小时候第一次去伦敦的大英博物馆时，我最喜欢的展品就是这尊 Moai。

sentences.en: In fact, it was the only photo I took at the museum on my old Nokia phone.
sentences.zh: 事实上，那是我用旧诺基亚手机在博物馆里拍的唯一一张照片。

sentences.en: From the British Museum’s perspective, their Moai statue is an important part of global heritage.
sentences.zh: 从大英博物馆的角度来看，他们的 Moai 雕像是全球遗产的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: They argue that displaying it allows people from around the world to learn about different cultures.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，将其展出可以让来自世界各地的人们了解不同的文化。

sentences.en: Museums like the British Museum often present themselves as protectors.
sentences.zh: 像大英博物馆这样的博物馆经常把自己包装成保护者。

sentences.en: They claim to be protecting or preserving artifacts that might be damaged or forgotten in other places.
sentences.zh: 他们声称自己是在保护或妥善保存那些在其他地方可能会损坏或被遗忘的文物。

sentences.en: But for the people of Rapa Nui, the story is different.
sentences.zh: 但对 Rapa Nui 人来说，故事则完全不同。

sentences.en: On Easter Island, the Moai are ancestors.
sentences.zh: 在复活节岛上，Moai 就是祖先。

sentences.en: They’re not art. They are the ancestors of the people.
sentences.zh: 它们不是艺术品，而是人民的祖先。

sentences.en: Removing them from the island is removing something very important.
sentences.zh: 把它们从岛上移走就是移走了某种非常重要的东西。

sentences.en: For many Rapa Nui, seeing their heritage displayed thousands of kilometers away is a reminder of a time when their voices were ignored.
sentences.zh: 对许多 Rapa Nui 人来说，看到他们的文化遗产在几千公里外展出，是在提醒他们那段声音被忽视的岁月。

sentences.en: Should museums have the right to keep objects taken during periods of inequality or colonial rule?
sentences.zh: 博物馆是否有权保留在不平等或殖民统治时期掠夺来的物品？

sentences.en: Similar debates surround the Parthenon marbles in London, or the Benin bronzes also in London and in Europe, and countless other artifacts around the world.
sentences.zh: 类似的争论也围绕着伦敦的帕台农神庙大理石雕刻，或是同样在伦敦和欧洲的贝宁青铜器，以及世界上的无数其他文物。

sentences.en: I have recorded previous episodes on this topic before as well.​
sentences.zh: 我以前也录制过关于这个主题的节目。​

sentences.en: Easter Island is one of the smallest and most isolated places on earth, but I find its story fascinating.
sentences.zh: 复活节岛是地球上最小、最孤立的地方之一，但我发现它的故事深深吸引着我。

sentences.en: By discussing the history of Easter Island, we have also talked about Polynesian expansion, potential Polynesian contact in South America, the mystery of the Moai, colonialism, and the debate over the ownership of history.
sentences.zh: 通过讨论复活节岛的历史，我们也谈到了波利尼西亚人的扩张、可能存在的波利尼西亚与南美洲接触、Moai 的谜团、殖民主义，以及关于历史所有权的争论。

sentences.en: But what do you think? Have you heard of Easter Island before?
sentences.zh: 但你怎么看？你以前听说过复活节岛吗？

sentences.en: Do you think it’s right for the British Museum to keep a Moai in its collection?
sentences.zh: 你认为大英博物馆在其藏品中保留一尊 Moai 是对的吗？

sentences.en: What is your opinion about museums holding important cultural artifacts from other cultures?
sentences.zh: 对于博物馆保存来自其他文化的贵重文化文物，你有什么看法？
